public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 279
*Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/279](https://www.erdosproblems.com/279)
-/

@[expose] public section

namespace Erdos279

/--
Let $k\geq 3$. Is there a choice of congruence classes $a_p\pmod{p}$ for every prime $p$
such that all sufficiently large integers can be written as $a_p+tp$ for some prime $p$
and integer $t\geq k$?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_279 :  answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ k : Nat, k ≥ 3 →
    ∃ a : Nat → Nat, ∃ N : Nat, (∀ p : Nat, p.Prime → a p < p) ∧
    ∀ n ≥ N, ∃ p : Nat, ∃ t ≥ k, p.Prime ∧ n = a p + t * p := by
  sorry

end Erdos279

reformulations.difference: The original Erdős–Graham formulation on p. 29 asks whether the primes give such a covering system for every k; Lean quantifies only over k ≥ 3.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: The covering property is downward monotone in k: the same residues and threshold work for a smaller k because t ≥ k' implies t ≥ k whenever k ≤ k'. Thus the case k = 3 supplies every omitted smaller k, and the universal statement over k ≥ 3 is equivalent to the universal statement over all natural (or positive integer) k. This equivalence was proved in /workspace/review/scratch.lean.

sources_consulted: P. Erdős and R. L. Graham, Old and New Problems and Results in Combinatorial Number Theory (1980), Chapter 3, pp. 24–29, especially p. 29 (PDF page 25): https://mathweb.ucsd.edu/~ronspubs/80_11_number_theory.pdf
review.notes: No mathematical defect found in the sole declaration. Checked quantifier scope, normalized residue representatives, Nat.Prime, the answer slot, and boundary cases. The scratch file compiles successfully and proves equivalence with a normalized integer-valued covering formulation, as well as equivalence of n = a + t*p with the appropriate congruence and size cutoff. The cited erdosproblems.com page repeatedly returned a Cloudflare challenge, so mathematical faithfulness was checked against the original book and its surrounding discussion instead. The independent Erdős Problems catalogue currently lists #279 as open, consistent with the file; the live site's latest remarks/status could not be inspected directly.
